title: A credit counter that can go negative is later used as a copy length, and the window that was meant to bound the write becomes the overflow
index_line: T-0093 · MEM_WRITE · HTTP/2 send-window underflow → invalid copy length → heap OOB in the nginx worker · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: Flow control is assumed to be a bound: the peer grants credit, the server never sends more than the credit allows, so the credit variable is a limit, not untrusted data. But the credit is adjusted by a peer-supplied delta and held in an unsigned counter — a reduction can wrap it, and the arithmetic that was supposed to forbid a copy then authorises an impossible one.

mechanism.does: an unauthenticated HTTP/2 client sends SETTINGS with a reduced SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE and/or WINDOW_UPDATE frames
nginx adjusts each active stream's remaining send credit by the difference between the old and new setting
a reduction drives the stream's unsigned send_window below zero, wrapping it to an enormous value instead of clamping at zero
the client cancels queued response data, and a later response is queued/copied using the invalid credit as a length
the resulting copy runs past the destination buffer, giving a heap out-of-bounds write (and a read for disclosure)
with heap shaping the corruption reaches control data, executing code with the nginx worker's privileges

source.protocol.value: HTTP/2 frames on an unauthenticated connection: SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, WINDOW_UPDATE, RST_STREAM, DATA

size.length.value: the send-window counter used as a permitted length after an unsigned underflow

sync.window.value: the per-stream and per-connection flow-control windows — the resource accounting that is supposed to bound the write

sink.memory.copy.value: the response-queue copy whose length comes from the corrupted window

preconditions.expr: HTTP/2 is enabled on a listening port

check.spec: curl -sI --http2 https://HOST/ | head -3; grep -rE 'listen .*http2|http2 on' /etc/nginx 2>/dev/null | head

preconditions.expr: the build is in the affected range (1.9.5 through 1.31.8)
the server returns DATA under HTTP/2 flow control (any content type; no backend needed)

success: worker crash or corrupted response under a crafted window sequence (many WINDOW_UPDATE frames on one long-lived connection, little data returned)
memory disclosure in a response body before control-flow hijack
failure_like: HTTP/2 disabled on the listening port
the build clamps the stream window at zero and rejects invalid SETTINGS deltas
false_positive: a worker restart under load is not this bug — require the frame sequence and the accounting anomaly (bytes_received climbing while bytes_sent stays low)
HTTP/2 probe support alone is reachability, not exploitability

hazards: every protocol with peer-granted credit (HTTP/2, HTTP/3, QUIC, SPDY, custom flow control): a credit counter is untrusted input
signed/unsigned mixed arithmetic in accounting code that later feeds a memcpy length
the guard that should have stopped the copy is the same value that was corrupted
non_transfers: implementations that clamp credit at zero and re-validate before each copy

provenance.author: Rapid7 (Vulnerability Research)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123007: HTTP/2 flow-control accounting; a SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE reduction changes each active stream window by the delta and can leave a stream with negative credit, the client cancels queued DATA and nginx later copies a response with an invalid length — CWE-191 integer underflow, worker-context RCE

provenance.author: Xint (nginx2root)
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123007: send-window arithmetic lets a window exceed its permitted maximum, producing an invalid memory-copy length and heap out-of-bounds read/write; ngx_http_v2_send_chain deducts from both h2c->send_window and stream->send_window; affects 1.9.5-1.31.8 and reaches RCE serving static files

provenance.author: MITRE / NIST NVD
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2026-123007 description (HTTP/2 flow-control window exceeding threshold → heap buffer overflow)
